summary: Verified allocation capacity calculation fix. Backend GET /api/allocations now returns weekly_hours for every allocation. Frontend correctly computes capacity as sum(weekly_hours)/max_weekly_hours. Akshaya=80%, Amrit=60% (not 120%), Bhavika=83% with Website Migration hours-type correctly showing 22h/wk. Summary stats: 5 Available / 2 At Capacity / 0 Over. No white-page crash on edit modal.

issues: For hours-type allocations, the row still shows the stored raw 'percentage' label (e.g., 55%) next to the correct '(22.0h/wk)' — the percentage label is misleading for hours-type allocations. Consider hiding the % or showing 'Fixed hours' badge instead when allocation_type='hours'.

action_items: (Optional/minor) For hours-type allocations on Allocations page, hide or clarify the raw stored percentage label since it's not meaningful once weekly_hours are correctly derived.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend fix in routes/allocations.py line 84-86 correctly calls allocation_weekly_hours(alloc, std_cap) using the canonical util. Rounded to 2 decimals.
Frontend Allocations.js getCapacityPct (lines 355-361) correctly uses sum(weekly_hours)/maxWeeklyHours. Timeline heatmap (line 291-294) also uses weekly_hours. Fix applied consistently.
allocation_weekly_hours() in utils.py handles both percentage and hours types canonically; percentage scales by standard_capacity, hours divides total_hours by weeks.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Allocation capacity fix verified end-to-end. Backend returns weekly_hours; frontend uses it. Amrit no longer shows 120%, Akshaya shows 80%, Bhavika hours-type correctly reflected in weekly hours. All 5 pytest tests passed. UI verified via Playwright with visual confirmation. Only minor cosmetic note: hours-type allocations still display the back-computed percentage next to weekly hours which can be confusing.
